messages:
rita: Heads-up: saw a customer thread where our Java SDK prefetch + auth rotation caused sustained 429s during onboarding. They had rotateInterval=5s and prefetch=5.

hao: Oof. Short-lived tokens + aggressive prefetch = thundering herd. Do we atomically release inflight when scheduling auth refresh?

rita: Looks like the auth refresh path acquires a client-wide lock but prefetch workers don't check that lock before issuing calls. So many warmup threads race and hit expired tokens -> 401 -> retry -> 429 from rate-limiter.

mentor-bot: heuristic alert: sdk.java.prefetch.auth-race triggered env=staging count=184 window=60s

infra: Immediate mitigation: recommend customers set rotateInterval>=30s for bulk ingest or reduce prefetch to 1. We'll add an onboarding note.

hao: Fix plan: 1) make prefetch check a client-level auth-refresh-in-progress flag and pause attempts; 2) ensure retry path decrements inflight counter before sleeping; 3) add jitter to warmup startup to avoid synchronized churn.

rita: Also propose adding a safety cap: if client observes >N 429s in M seconds, automatically throttle prefetch to 1 and emit sdk.prefetch.autothrottle event.

mentor-bot: suggestion: add unit test that simulates token rotate every 3s and asserts no leak in inflight and no duplicates.

infra: We'll also expose metrics: sdk.java.inflight, sdk.java.auth.refreshing, sdk.java.prefetch.paused so SRE can alert earlier.

hao: I'll open PR fix/java-prefetch-auth-jitter with the change and tests. If small, we can cherry-pick to a patch release.

rita: Thanks. I'll follow up with comms to Customer Success and update Quickstart FAQ about token rotation guidance.
